summary: Implemented the Device/DeviceService/DeviceType domain models with input validation (host/port/username/name), and a JsonDeviceRepository persisting devices.json with the same atomic-write and corrupted-file-quarantine pattern established for config.json in WU003. Individual invalid devices are dropped (with a warning) on load rather than failing the whole file. Added get_devices/get_device Tauri commands and TypeScript mirror types/wrappers. 18 new Rust unit tests, 31 total passing.
completed: domain/device.rs: Device/DeviceService structs matching the architecture spec's domain model; DeviceType serializes as kebab-case.

Device::validate(): non-empty name; host must be a valid IPv4/IPv6 address or well-formed hostname with shell metacharacters/whitespace rejected; ssh_port must be non-zero; ssh_username must be a POSIX-style lowercase identifier.

storage/device_repository.rs: DeviceRepository trait + JsonDeviceRepository. load_all() never fails (missing -> empty list; corrupted -> quarantined + empty list; individual invalid devices dropped with a warning, valid ones kept). save_all() writes the {schemaVersion, devices} envelope atomically.
commands/devices.rs: get_devices / get_device Tauri commands, registered in lib.rs.
src/types/device.ts + src/lib/tauri/devices.ts: TypeScript mirror types and typed wrappers.
Marked save_all()/DEVICES_SCHEMA_VERSION #[allow(dead_code)] since they're exercised by tests but not yet called from a command -- create/update/delete land in WU006.
18 new Rust unit tests (13 domain validation + kebab-case serialization, 5 repository including malformed-JSON recovery and mixed-validity file handling).
Verified cargo test (31/31), cargo build, npm run build, and npm run lint all pass.

validationCommands.summary: Clean build, no warnings after adding targeted #[allow(dead_code)] on the not-yet-wired save path.
tsc + vite build succeeded with the new device types/wrapper included.
0 errors, same 2 pre-existing HMR-granularity warnings as WU004.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Devices persist across an application restart
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: save_then_load_round_trips repository test: save_all() then load_all() returns the identical device list.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: devices.json includes schemaVersion and validates on load
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: DevicesFile wraps { schemaVersion, devices }; malformed JSON is quarantined and recovered to an empty list rather than crashing (load_recovers_from_malformed_json test).

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Rust unit tests cover domain validation rules (host, port, username format)
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: 13 domain::device tests cover valid/invalid host (empty, shell metacharacters, malformed label, IPv4, IPv6), port (zero, max), username (uppercase, digit-first, shell metacharacters), and empty name.

notes: Risk score: 20/100 (low). Rationale: purely additive domain/storage/read-command code with no SSH or network surface yet; the security-relevant part (rejecting shell metacharacters in host/username so a later terminal-launch or SSH command can't be built via string interpolation) is directly unit-tested rather than assumed.

get_devices/get_device are read-only in this work unit per its explicit scope; create_device/update_device/delete_device (which will call save_all()) and their own input-validation-to-ApplicationError wiring are WU006.
